links.outcome: Patient-rated readability and comprehensibility of AI plain-language MRI summaries versus original reports; Flesch-Kincaid score
links.effect: Patients rated AI summaries higher for readability (median 5 vs 2, p=0.011) and comprehensibility (5 vs 2, p=0.007); Flesch-Kincaid 54.6 vs 32.2 (p=0.005); no clinically significant inaccuracies.
links.quote: Patients rated AI summaries significantly higher in readability (median 5 vs. 2, p = 0.011), comprehensibility (5 vs. 2, p = 0.007), utility (5 vs. 3, p = 0.014), and overall quality (4.5 vs. 4, p = 0.013), with fewer follow-up questions (3 vs. 4, p = 0.018).

screen.reason: The study evaluates the performance, accuracy, and patient/clinician perception of AI-generated patient-friendly MRI summaries compared to standard reports, rather than evaluating a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
